$schema_note: THE PROVIDERS TABLE (providers.yaml-style, JSON because the kit is stdlib-only): one row per provider. Adding Google/OpenRouter/Groq-class providers is a data edit here, never new code in key_wizard.py. Fields: name, flow (device|manual|<future oauth flows>), scopes (space-joined at request time), device_code_endpoint + token_endpoint (device flow), allowed_hosts (the endpoint fence allowlist - the wizard refuses any URL whose host is not exactly here), env_key (the .env name the token is stored under), client_id_env (env var holding the app's client_id for device flow), interval_default (RFC 8628: 5 when omitted), expires_in_default, console_url (manual flow; all four URLs curl-verified 200 on 2026-10-07), enabled. Only enabled rows are runnable; disabled rows are data for the later stretch (the agent-navigates-console version stays OUT - fragile and ToS-sensitive per provider; the sanctioned mirror is the provider's own OAuth/device grant with user consent).

providers.name: github
providers.notes: Create an OAuth App at console_url, check 'Enable Device Flow', put its Client ID in KEY_WIZARD_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID. Device flow needs client_id only, no client secret. Endpoints + grant_type + 900s expiry per GitHub docs (curl-verified 2026-10-07).

providers.name: google
providers.notes: DATA ROW ONLY: v0 wizard implements device + manual flows and refuses this one by name. Google AI Studio issues plain API keys (manual paste works today via flow 'manual' once enabled); the loopback OAuth flow is the later stretch. Fill endpoints from Google's OAuth docs before enabling.

providers.name: openrouter
providers.notes: DATA ROW ONLY: PKCE web flow is not implemented in v0; keys are pasted manually today (enable flow 'manual'). Fill endpoints from OpenRouter's OAuth docs before enabling.

providers.name: groq
providers.notes: Groq issues console keys, no OAuth: the manual flow (prompt -> hidden paste -> .env) is the sanctioned path, zero network in the wizard.
